g1|variants|quantity contract.summary: A quantity contract is a binding long-term sales agreement where a customer commits to purchasing a specific total quantity of material over a defined validity period. Variants differ by pricing determination, fulfillment mechanics with or without subsequent delivery creation, and release order integration.

variants.when_used: Standard long-term agreement where releases are processed via sales orders leading to outbound deliveries and billing.

variants.when_used: Agreements where contract releases or direct service executions bypass shipping and bill directly from the order or contract state.

g1|core|quantity contract|standard quant.title: Standard Quantity Contract with Delivery
g1|core|quantity contract|standard quant.story: Imagine a giant balloon factory that promises to sell a customer a thousand water balloons over the year, writing down the exact number on a special agreement scroll so neither side forgets. In SAP S/4HANA, a Quantity Contract (sales document type MK) is a legal pre-sale agreement where a customer commits to purchase a specific total quantity of material within a defined validity period, serving as the master outline from which subsequent release orders, outbound deliveries, and delivery-related billings are drawn.
g1|core|quantity contract|standard quant.why_business_needs_it: This scenario allows businesses to lock in long-term customer commitments and secure guaranteed sales volume while offering tiered pricing and streamlined fulfillment. It prevents administrative overhead by avoiding the creation of independent sales orders from scratch every time the customer needs a partial shipment.

g1|core|quantity contract|value-quant mi.title: Value-Quant Mixed Quantity Contract (Quantity Contract WK1)
g1|core|quantity contract|value-quant mi.story:
Imagine a giant toy store agrees to buy one thousand toy cars over the year, and you promise to lock in a special low price for that whole batch. In SAP, this agreement is captured in a special sales document called a quantity contract, which tracks how many cars the customer has ordered so far against their total limit. When the customer is ready for some cars, you create regular sales orders referencing that contract, and the system automatically checks that they do not buy more than their agreed limit. This specific variant, the Value-Quant Mixed Quantity Contract (contract type WK1 with item category WVN), ties the target quantity and value checks to a pricing reference material while billing based on outbound deliveries.

A Quantity Contract (Sales Document Type WK1) is a legal binding agreement where a customer commits to purchase a specific quantity or value of materials within a defined validity period, acting as an outline agreement that absorbs subsequent release orders (calls-off) up to the target quantity, utilizing delivery-related billing (Billing Relevance F).
g1|core|quantity contract|value-quant mi.why_business_needs_it: Businesses use quantity contracts to secure long-term customer commitments and offer tiered pricing while managing fulfillment and credit control through subsequent deliveries. It prevents unauthorized discounting by binding release orders directly to the agreed framework agreement terms.

g1|core|quantity contract|quantity contr.title: Quantity Contract without Delivery (Direct Billing)
g1|core|quantity contract|quantity contr.story: Imagine a giant agreement where a customer promises to buy a specific total quantity of items over a year, and instead of shipping every little piece with a delivery document, the company just bills the customer directly as orders roll in. In SAP S/4HANA Sales, a quantity contract (document type MK) holds this target quantity, and subsequent sales orders or direct billing documents draw down against that target without requiring a Logistics Execution outbound delivery.
g1|core|quantity contract|quantity contr.why_business_needs_it: This setup allows businesses to lock in long-term sales commitments and volume targets with major clients while streamlining the billing process for services or goods where formal warehouse delivery documents add unnecessary administrative overhead. It guarantees accurate quantity tracking against the contract release without triggering inventory movements or warehouse tasks.

g1|core|quantity contract|intercompany q.title: Intercompany Quantity Contract Fulfillment
g1|core|quantity contract|intercompany q.story: Imagine a giant toy store group where one company sells the toys, but another company actually ships them from a different warehouse. In SAP, we set up an Intercompany Quantity Contract so a customer can sign a legally binding deal for a total number of items, and the supplying company handles the deliveries and billing across company codes automatically. g1|panel|quantity contract.otc_impact: Quantity contracts sit at the upstream boundary of Order-to-Cash, establishing legally binding target quantities and validity periods that govern subsequent release orders. This family impacts OTC by transforming unpredictable customer demand into controlled, scheduled fulfillment streams while automating pricing agreements, target quantity checks, and billing document creation. Integration spans sales document creation, dynamic delivery scheduling, subsequent outbound delivery processing, and final billing generation.

panel_qa.question: How do we handle over-delivery on quantity contracts without disrupting customer relationships?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Quantity contracts rely on target quantity checks defined at the scheduling agreement or contract item level to control subsequent release orders. When a release order causes cumulative issued quantities to exceed the target quantity, SAP triggers error message V1 355 or warning V1 356 depending on the completion rule configuration in Customizing. Business users manage this through transaction VA42 by either renegotiating contract extensions or establishing a follow-up contract document. This control prevents revenue leakage and enforces contractual compliance while giving customer service teams visibility into consumption rates. We configure over-delivery tolerances in the item category via transaction VOV7 to balance strict financial controls with flexible customer service. Next, we monitor contract consumption through standard analytics apps like Sales Contract Fulfillment Rates.
panel_qa.trap: Customizing manual z-tables to track contract balances outside of standard sales document flow.

panel_qa.question: What is the architectural trade-off between Quantity Contract without Delivery and standard delivery-relevant contracts?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Standard quantity contracts use delivery-relevant item categories like TAC, requiring an outbound delivery via transaction VL01N and Goods Issue prior to billing, ensuring physical inventory is tracked. Quantity contracts without delivery use billing-relevant item categories like TAX, bypassing Logistics Execution and posting directly from the contract to Financial Accounting via transaction VF01. We choose the direct billing variant for service-based agreements or digital goods where physical warehouse movements do not occur, reducing document overhead and eliminating unnecessary delivery processing steps. The key configuration lies in setting the billing relevance indicator on item category TAX to 'B' (A/R billing from sales document) in transaction VOV7. This ensures accurate revenue recognition while decoupling OTC from warehouse dependencies. Next, we validate that pricing types on copy controls between contract and billing document maintain correct baseline conditions.
panel_qa.trap: Forcing physical delivery documents for non-material or milestone-based service contracts.

panel_qa.question: How does the intercompany quantity contract fulfillment scenario impact DSO and revenue recognition?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Intercompany quantity contracts involve a selling company code that captures the customer contract and an issuing company code that delivers the goods from its plant. This process uses cross-company billing where the issuing plant bills the selling company via intercompany billing document type IV, and the selling company bills the end customer via document type F2. We configure this via customer-vendor linking in customer master data (XD01/BP) and automatic intercompany billing settings in transaction VTAA and VTFL. The leadership value is maintaining clean statutory books across multiple legal entities while satisfying the customer with a single point of invoicing and delivery. This structure ensures accurate Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) tracking and compliant intercompany profit elimination during month-end close. Next, we ensure output determination for intercompany invoice transmission operates without manual intervention.
panel_qa.trap: Creating separate customer-facing contracts for each participating company code instead of using intercompany determination.

panel_qa.question: What happens to open quantity contracts when pricing conditions change mid-term?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Pricing updates on active quantity contracts depend on the price-source configuration in the sales document type and pricing type rules in copy control. When a price condition record changes in transaction VK11, existing contracts do not automatically re-price unless manual update or pricing type 'B' (Carry out new pricing) is invoked during release order creation. We configure pricing determination via transaction VOR1 and VOR2 to ensure contractual price protection clauses are honored for agreed validity periods. This prevents audit findings regarding unauthorized price increases on locked-in corporate supply agreements. Next, we run mass pricing updates using transaction VKP0 or custom batch programs if contractual indexing requires system-wide adjustments.
panel_qa.trap: Assuming that changing a condition record in VK11 instantly alters the net value of all open release orders.

panel_qa.question: How do we prevent duplicate release orders from depleting the same contract quantity concurrently?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Concurrent release order creation from the same quantity contract is managed by SAP's internal document locking mechanisms and update task sequencing. When multiple users create release orders simultaneously using transaction VA01, table VBUP and VBEP are locked, ensuring cumulative target quantity checks read up-to-date committed quantities. We configure incompletion procedures via transaction VOFM and ensure schedule line categories correctly update the open quantity fields. This prevents inventory overallocation and avoids customer disputes regarding unfulfilled contract balances. Next, we implement SAP Credit Management integration to hold release orders if the customer exceeds credit exposure limits.
panel_qa.trap: Relying on offline spreadsheets to track contract consumption alongside SAP.

panel_qa.question: What is the exact financial and logistical impact of cancelling a quantity contract with incomplete billing?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Cancelling a quantity contract requires setting rejection reasons at the item level via transaction VA42, which immediately releases reserved inventory and updates status fields in table VBUK. When an item is rejected, open schedule lines are zeroed out, preventing any further outbound deliveries or billing documents from referencing that contract item. The financial impact is immediate reversal of unbilled backlog metrics and clearing of open order values from credit management exposure. We configure rejection reasons in transaction OVAG to control whether rejected items can still be billed or if they are permanently closed. Next, we run reporting via VA05N to verify that all terminated contracts display complete status indicators.
panel_qa.trap: Deleting contract items physically instead of applying standard rejection reasons, which corrupts document audit trails.
